canonical_definition: Hallucination Propensity refers to the tendency of AI models, particularly large language models, to generate content that is plausible-sounding but false, fabricated, or unsupported by evidence, often manifesting in open-ended generation, long-form question answering, or retrieval-augmented tasks. This propensity is associated with reduced factual accuracy, may involve incorrect object references or attention patterns in multimodal settings, and is sometimes linked to a lack of supporting evidence in inputs or decreased capability. Some definitions emphasize its role in misinformation risks, while others highlight its mitigation through validation mechanisms or confidence indicators.
